question: Should Discord Activity support be rebuilt under the Canvas/Discord plugin contracts with fail-closed Activity auth, continued through the newer overlapping branch after repair, or paused until the Activity security model is settled?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, operator config shape, and overlapping open branches, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through newer branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave Discord Activities out until maintainers settle whether the security model belongs in the Canvas plugin, Discord plugin, or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking decision is primarily about Gateway auth, config migration, and Canvas plugin ownership, where recent current-main history points to this owner-boundary work.
